newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Fifteen banks join the effort to assure depositors. Financial authorities enlisted the support of the country's commercial banks in an all-out effort to assure customers their deposits with finance houses are safe. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh stressed the point in a televised address last night. He said the government will guarantee the deposits and debts of finance companies, both in Thailand and overseas. (BANGKOK POST).

- Despite prevailing criticism, prime minister Chavalit insisted that Thailand's economic slump had reached its lowest point and the economy was now on the rise. Chavalit said in a television interview that no more firms would be shut down following the forced closure of 16 failed companies last week. He also committed himself to further defending the baht against speculative attack, saying the national currency could never be devalued. (THE NATION)

- The opposition Democrats are vowing to push for a 45 billion baht cut to the budget bill during the scrutiny process. The planned cut of 45 billion baht from the 982 billion baht budget for fiscal 1998 would be kept as a central fund for necessary uses, said Pichet Phanvichartkul, deputy chairman of the budget scrutiny committee. (BANGKOK POST).

- Drug trafficking is a major cause of unrest and social and economic problems in southern border provinces, the Fourth Army Region commander said. Lieutenant-General Preecha Suwannasri said the unrest, including arson and bomb blasts, were caused by conflicts among drug gangs. (BANGKOK POST)

- Foreign currency speculators are likely to return and attack the baht in August, when three-and six- month forward contracts close, warned Siam Commercial bank president Olarn Chaipravat. Olarn said once forward contracts taken during an attack on the currency in mid-May were closed, the baht would remain open for a renewed attack. (BANGKOK POST)

- After the financial crisis heat fever pitch on Friday due to the Bank of Thailand merger measures, stock analysts remained wary of unexpected factors which might hamper the stock market. The central bank's long-awaited surgery on the finance company sector, forcing 16 finance companies to institute mergers with stronger ones, is expected to calm things down and brighten the future prospects of the financial industry. (THE NATION).

- Even though Lehman Brothers maintains that Thailad's economic fundamentals do not warrnat a signficant baht devaluation, it is predicting low gross domestic product growth this year following the tight currency policy. (THE NATION)
